dimension.category_description: Visible rules or boundaries that restrict generation, protect artifact regions, preserve privacy, or reserve part of the task for the user.
dimension.classification_boundary: The constraint must be expressed through the interface or directly shape an observable interaction; invisible policies are excluded.

candidates.title: From Conversation to Human-AI Common Ground: Extracting Cognitive Workflows for Reuse in Sense-making Tasks
candidates.why: A reusable, independently defined schema requires extracted workflows to take the form of dependency-linked phases with explicit inputs, activities, decisions, and outputs. It is a particularly strong exemplar because the template captures the structure of reasoning itself, not merely the formatting of a response.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: It ranks above IntelliCircos because its phase-and-dependency schema is substantially more transferable across domains while remaining explicit enough to reconstruct.
candidates.pattern_summary: A structure declared in advance — a schema, slot set, section skeleton, or typed taxonomy — determines the form the model's output must take.
candidates.structural_signature: A named structure with enumerated parts (fields, sections, component types, category labels) is defined independently of any single generation and is stored in the system. The generator's output is emitted into, checked against, or parsed by that structure, and downstream rendering is per-part: each part gets its own visual slot, colour, or handle. Outputs that do not conform are corrected or rejected before display.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: I departed from the consensus by moving rid 623 from fifth to second and excluding consensus runner-up rid 6089. IntelliCircos received a +0.27 adjustment because its quoted evidence most fully exposes a reconstructable structural signature: named types, delimiters, nesting, cardinality, separation, and ordering. Rid 9312 received a small uplift because the template is visibly selected before generation and determines section-level output. Rid 6089 was excluded because its quote establishes a JSON field contract but does not show per-field rendering, validation, rejection, or correction; it is valid but comparatively close to ordinary structured-response formatting. Readers should distrust any stronger claims about validation or downstream rendering for all three picks: none of the supplied excerpts explicitly documents rejection or correction of nonconforming outputs, and the rendering implication is strongest—but still partly inferred—for IntelliCircos. The evidence for rid 5176 also establishes schema extraction and reuse more clearly than it establishes enforcement during every generation.

candidates.title: IntelliCircos: A Data-driven and AI-powered Authoring Tool for Circos Plots
candidates.why: The system defines a concrete generative grammar with fixed start and end markers, named CIRCOS, RING, and TRACK elements, nesting and cardinality rules, separators, and an outside-to-inside ordering constraint. This is the clearest evidence among the candidates of an output being parseable—and therefore checkable and renderable—against a stored structural contract.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: It ranks above the narrative-writing system because its evidence specifies the template's delimiters, hierarchy, multiplicity, and ordering, whereas the narrative-schema quote establishes sections and functions but not conformance mechanics.

candidates.title: From Text-First to Structure-First: A Visual Pipeline for Narrative Writing
candidates.why: Writers visibly choose a reusable narrative schema before generation, and that schema predetermines both the output sections and the function each section must serve. It cleanly demonstrates the section-skeleton form of Output Templates as an interaction-level constraint rather than a hidden prompt convention.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: It ranks above Just-In-Time Objectives because selecting a stored schema visibly governs the organization and semantic roles of the generated artifact, while the JSON example only evidences three response fields and their value constraints.

candidates.title: ConstitutionMaker: Interactively Critiquing Large Language Models by Converting Feedback into Principles
candidates.why: ConstitutionMaker turns user feedback into an accumulated, named constitution of principles that governs later model behavior, closely matching the pattern’s user-authored collection and persistent-policy mechanism.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: Chosen over Policy Maps because converting feedback into a named constitution more directly realizes an inspectable standing rule set, while the runner-up organizes policies spatially and does not establish persistence.
candidates.pattern_summary: The user builds up a standing set of rules, principles, or preferences that is stored outside any single generation and consulted on every subsequent run.
candidates.structural_signature: A named collection with add / edit / remove / reorder operations, persisted across generations and rendered as a list. Each entry originates from a user act (typed preference, feedback on an output converted into a rule, an imported written protocol) and is compiled into something the generator consults — a prompt fragment, an executable predicate, a decoding constraint, an ordering. Priority among entries may be expressed by position in the list rather than by numeric weight.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: The final membership and order follow the consensus, but the scores for Policy Maps and Semantic Commit are modestly reduced because each proves only one side of the structural signature especially well: Policy Maps shows authoring and execution but not persistence or conventional list management, while Semantic Commit shows accumulation and list structure but not the compilation-and-consultation path. No adjustment exceeds 0.3. Readers should distrust claims about add/edit/remove/reorder operations and cross-generation persistence unless confirmed in the full papers: the supplied evidence consists of short abstract or introduction excerpts and does not directly document those details. ConstitutionMaker is the strongest pick, although even its excerpt does not explicitly show list operations or priority handling.

candidates.title: Policy Maps: Tools for Guiding the Unbounded Space of LLM Behaviors
candidates.why: Policy Projector lets practitioners define custom semantic regions and author explicit if-then rules whose actions are applied to LLM outputs, making the compilation and enforcement of user policy unusually concrete.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: Chosen over Semantic Commit because it demonstrates the complete authoring-to-execution path, whereas the runner-up establishes an accumulated specification list but not how agents operationalize its entries.

candidates.title: ClassMeta: Designing Interactive Virtual Classmate to Promote VR Classroom Participation
candidates.why: ClassMeta deliberately stops at a partial answer and makes the student supply its completion, directly realizing the truncated-pipeline structure in an observable interaction.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: It ranks above rid 3547 because withholding part of an answer and soliciting its completion demonstrates the human-supplied terminal step more literally than correctness-only feedback.
candidates.pattern_summary: The system runs the pipeline that would produce a terminal output but does not emit that output.
candidates.structural_signature: The last stage of the pipeline is truncated at the presentation boundary: what reaches the screen is an intermediate of the process whose end product is withheld, and the interface exposes no control that reveals it. The user's action supplies the terminal value, so the loop cannot close without a human act.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: I departed from the consensus by moving rid 3208 to first and excluding consensus leader rid 2257. I would adjust rid 2257 downward by more than 0.3 (from 4.67 to roughly 4.25) because its quote shows an unanswered question but does not establish the structural signature's computed-but-withheld terminal output or the absence of a reveal path. The selected evidence is still limited: none of the excerpts proves that no reveal control exists; rid 3208 states an intended participation benefit rather than a measured effect; rid 3547 does not isolate the effect of answer withholding; and rid 13637 does not prove that generating proposed changes is technically part of the same pipeline. Rid 13637 was retained despite that caveat because it supplies a strong non-educational instance of exposing diagnostic intermediates while reserving the final intervention for the user.

candidates.why: The system emits the penultimate result—whether the response is correct—but withholds the correct answer after an error, requiring the learner to determine it independently.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: It ranks above rid 13637 because the withheld terminal value and the learner's responsibility to supply it are explicit, whereas conflict highlighting does not prove that suggested edits are an existing final pipeline stage.

candidates.title: Style2Fab: Functionality-Aware Segmentation for Fabricating Personalized 3D Models with Generative AI
candidates.why: Style2Fab is the cleanest canonical exemplar: functionality-aware segmentation computes a protected set of functional geometry, while generation is restricted to the mutable aesthetic complement so personalization cannot compromise the object’s use.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: Chosen over CICADA because its inferred semantic partition and protection of fabrication-critical geometry embody both halves of the pattern more centrally and consequentially than provenance-based preservation in a system studied primarily for perceived agency.
candidates.pattern_summary: Part of the working artifact is designated off-limits and the generator is prevented from altering it, with the designation produced by the system rather than drawn by the user.
candidates.structural_signature: The artifact is partitioned into a protected subset and a mutable subset; the partition is computed (by segmentation, or by provenance of who authored each element) rather than selected; generation is then executed under a constraint or penalty that forbids modifying, overwriting or occluding the protected subset. Two things are needed and both are observable: an automatic partition step, and an enforcement mechanism at generation time. Transplants to text (generate around the user's own sentences), code (do not touch hand-written blocks), layout, audio.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: I departed from the consensus by placing Style2Fab first: although CICADA has clearer mechanism evidence, Style2Fab is more central to the pattern and better demonstrates a system-inferred semantic protected region with consequential functional stakes. No score was adjusted by more than 0.3. Only two candidate records were actually provided, despite the prompt saying there were three, so a defensible third exemplar cannot be selected without inventing metadata or evidence. Readers should treat Style2Fab’s evidence cautiously: the automatic partition is inferred partly from the title, and the abstract quote does not reveal the exact enforcement mechanism. CICADA is supported by a single system-description excerpt, and the paper’s principal contribution appears to concern perceptions of agency rather than Protected Region itself.

candidates.title: When is a Tool a Tool? User Perceptions of System Agency in Human-AI Co-Creative Drawing
candidates.why: CICADA provides exceptionally explicit provenance-based protection: the system treats user-authored strokes as the protected subset and applies a generation-time penalty against moving, overdrawing, or visually occluding them.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: It outranks any further selection because no third candidate record was supplied, while its evidence directly establishes both the automatic provenance partition and generation-time enforcement required by the structural signature.

candidates.title: CreativeConnect: Supporting Reference Recombination for Graphic Design Ideation with Generative AI
candidates.why: This is a near-definitional exemplar: every system-generated recombination is uniformly limited to a line sketch and one-line description, explicitly leaving users to supply specificity through reinterpretation.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: Unlike Inkspire, CreativeConnect’s evidence establishes the uniform ceiling, identifies both sparse output forms, and explicitly connects withheld detail to user reinterpretation.
candidates.pattern_name: Low Detail Outlines with User-Filled Specificity
candidates.pattern_summary: The system renders its output below the fidelity it could achieve, using a sparse representation and minimal accompanying text.
candidates.structural_signature: A ceiling is imposed on the rendering stage: outputs are emitted in a low-detail representation (outline instead of full render, one line instead of a paragraph) uniformly across all outputs, with no affordance to raise the fidelity. The invariant is that the representation underdetermines the artifact — many finished artifacts are consistent with what is shown. Transplants to wireframes instead of mockups, outlines instead of prose, thumbnails instead of masters.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: I preserved the consensus order but materially reduced Quologue from 1.95 to 1.3 because its evidence does not satisfy the structural signature: it removes contextual metadata rather than imposing a rendering-stage fidelity ceiling. It is best treated as a negative boundary case, so the supplied pool supports only two defensible positive exemplars. Inkspire is also weakly evidenced: its short feature description does not prove a uniform ceiling, lack of a higher-fidelity option, or explicit user completion. CreativeConnect is the only selection whose quote directly establishes the complete mechanism; even there, the evidence states design intent rather than measured impact.

candidates.title: Inkspire: Supporting Design Exploration with Generative AI through Analogical Sketching
candidates.why: Converting AI designs into lower-fidelity sketch scaffolding matches the central move of withholding finish so users can continue elaborating, although the evidence does not establish that this ceiling is uniform or unavoidable.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: Inkspire at least transforms generated artifacts into incomplete sketch scaffolds, whereas Quologue removes contextual anchors to stimulate reflection rather than producing low-detail artifacts for users to finish.
